Olga (eng-ml): Heads up — onboarding Zephyr -> Orpheus conversion turned up a tiny but consistent top-k drop after INT4 quant. Suspect tokenizer normalization + rotary handshake offset. Repro below. :thinking:

Olga (eng-ml): quick numbers: LTQA-small prompts, fp16 acc@1 0.842 -> int4 0.833 (delta -0.009). Not catastrophic but reproducible across seeds.

Sam (mlinfra): can you paste a minimal repro (token ids before/after)?

Olga (eng-ml): sure. gist of the failing case: some inputs with diacritics/zwj produce different token sequences between the on-disk vocab and our tokenizer codepath. snippet:

```
# zephyr tokenizer (on-disk vocab)
>>> tokenizer.encode("na\u00efve")
[11234, 903, 44]
# orpheus tokenizer (runtime state)
>>> tokenizer.encode("na\u00efve")
[11234, 789, 44]  # middle token differs
```

Olga (eng-ml): That single token id swap cascades: kvcache indexing shifts for subsequent tokens -> rotary phase uses wrong index. After quantization (int4) the numerical brittleness amplifies small phase misalignment into top-k differences.

Kevin (eng-runtime): interesting. two separate issues colliding: tokenizer canonicalization vs rotary index alignment. Did you check whether normalizing input fixes it?

Olga (eng-ml): quick test: applying NFKC pre-normalize before tokenization recovers the fp16 baseline in most cases. Example:

```
>>> import unicodedata
>>> s = "e\u000301"  # composed vs decomposed
>>> unicodedata.normalize('NFKC', s)
# then tokenizer.encode(...) matches on-disk sequence
```

Olga (eng-ml): With nfkc pre-normalize, int4 acc@1 -> 0.840 (delta -0.002). Remaining diffs are mainly ZWJ and soft-hyphen combos.

Luca (product): is nfkc pre-normalize safe as a short-term compat shim? any downstream compatibility risk?

Sam (mlinfra): short-term yes, long-term we should unify vocab/tokenizer artifacts. We can't silently change client-side behavior for hosted API without a flag. For Dedicated/Private we can turn on compat layer per-tenant.

Kevin (eng-runtime): other mitigation: runtime can detect kvcache misalignment by comparing predicted vs observed cache-hit distribution per-head and try a rotary-offset fallback (shift by +/-1 head index) before committing tokens. Might be cheap.

Olga (eng-ml): I instrumented a small probe: when token id mismatch occurs at token i, the per-head kv dot-product distribution shows a lag spike at i+1. Script output: 

```
# probe output (short)
probe: mismatch_count=14/1000
lagged_heads=[2,5]
mean_topk_delta=0.008
```

Sam (mlinfra): plan proposal: 1) add nfkc pre-normalize as an opt-in compat layer in model-metadata on import (private/dedicated default on for now), 2) upstream tokenizer PR to canonicalize stored vocab and publish migration guide, 3) add a lightweight runtime probe + rotary-offset fallback when probe rate > threshold.

Olga (eng-ml): implemented a quick import-time checker (detects ZWJ/combining-char token splits) and emits warnings. I'll open the tokenizer PR after we triage the rare soft-hyphen cases.

Kevin (eng-runtime): I'll spec a unit test that fails the runtime build if a new model import produces >0.5% token-id divergence for our canonical tokenizer vs on-disk vocab (so we catch regressions).

ci-bot: deploy job started for branch nfkc-compat-shim (#432) :gear:

Sam (mlinfra): thanks ci-bot :pray: I'll run the full chair-bench suite across Zephyr/Orpheus variants tonight and paste a summary.

Olga (eng-ml): one more note — quantized kernels amplify rotary-phase drift more than fp16; so even if we patch vocab, we should re-run int4 calibration with the canonical tokenizer to be safe.

Luca (product): good catch. let's table broad rollout until we have both import shim + runtime probe. Prioritize enterprise customers who hit this.

Sam (mlinfra): will do. I'll also add an opt-in API header for clients to request strict-tokenizer=false to preserve legacy behaviour while we migrate.

Olga (eng-ml): filing the tracking TODOs in the onboarding checklist and adding failing example set to the model package. will push PRs shortly.

Kevin (eng-runtime): ping me when you have the failing example set. I'll wire the test and the rotary-fallback experiment.

Olga (eng-ml): thanks — sending small repro in the PR. :thumbsup:
